purpose: Independent visual check of two corrections proposed by the structure reviewer; no edits to that reviewer ledger.
method: Compared full primary Texts PDF120/printed109 and enlarged crops directly with explicitly numbered primary sign-list glyphs. Correction alternatives were disclosed in the task, so the review is independent but not blind.

records.confidence: high for M402 versus M178 morphology
reasons: Printed second sign has one long oblique stem extending above and below a small right-attached triangular flag with internal subdivision. It matches numbered M402 (PDF46, printed35).
Numbered M178 (PDF44, printed33) is an A-like two-leg form whose right leg ends in small terminal branches. The primary 4359 sign does not have that two-legged outline.
The rightmost diamond with radiating upper strokes matches numbered M272. RTL-normalized complete line is M272 M402.

records.confidence: high for M226 versus M216 morphology
reasons: Printed disputed sign has a closed triangular left portion and two branches extending right. Its upper-right branch has a terminal down-and-up bend, while the lower-right branch is plain and straight. This matches numbered M226 (PDF45, printed34).
Numbered M216 (PDF44, printed33) has bent terminals on both right branches. The primary 4370 sign does not have the lower terminal bend required for that identification.
The other glyphs match the spoked oval M391, two short upper-position strokes M099, and offset three-bar enclosure M254. RTL-normalized complete line is M391 M099 M226 M254.

limits: This confirms editorial glyph identity and transcription, not the physical artifact, phonetics, semantics, or equivalence across other sign-numbering systems.
Enlargement adds no source detail; complete page is retained with reference labels and metadata.
